html:
The Wassoulou Empire was the state built by the Malinke leader Samori Ture in the savanna of what are now Guinea, southern Mali and northern Ivory Coast, from about 1878 to 1898. The map shows it in its 1880 snapshot, near its founding.

Samori came from a family of Dyula traders. He became a war leader in the 1860s, built a professional army, and by 1878 ruled a large realm from Bissandugu. He governed it as a Muslim state, taking the title almamy in 1884. His smiths learned to copy and repair European rifles, and he bought modern guns through Sierra Leone.

From 1882 he fought the French, who were pushing east from Senegal. He signed treaties, then fought again. In the 1890s, losing his western lands, he moved his whole state east, which the map shows as the First and Second Samori Empires. The French captured him in 1898, and he died in exile in Gabon in 1900. He is remembered as one of the great resisters of colonial conquest.
